bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, building systems that learn from data and improve without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: trains on labeled data to predict continuous (regression) or categorical (classification) outputs.
Unsupervised Learning: trains on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (clustering, dimensionality reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: agent learns by interacting with environment to maximize rewards (robotics, gaming).
Model Training: feeding data to learn patterns and minimize prediction differences.
Features and Labels: input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: model is too simple, fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: models linear relationship for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: predicts class probability for classification tasks.
Decision Trees: non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): finds optimal hyperplane for classification, effective in high-dimensional spaces.
Neural Networks: inspired by human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatments.
Finance: fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: evaluate model performance using separate datasets.
Metrics for classification: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score.
Metrics for regression: mean squared error (MSE), R-squared.
Cross-Validation: technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: optimizing model settings for optimal performance using grid/random search.
Data Quality and Quantity: models need large amounts of accurate, consistent data; labeled data collection is challenging.
Interpretability: complex models are difficult to understand, problematic in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: common issues where models learn noise or are too simple.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
ML applications will become more integrated into daily life (healthcare, education, transportation).
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
